what: Does tt-metal v0.77.0's tt-train stability set (#48716) improve tt-tnt's validation loss?
answer: SUPERSEDED -- see FINAL_2026-08-19_at_11_points. No measurable difference across 11 matched points.

comparison.candidate: artifacts/checkpoints-v077 -- beta2 0.95, weight_decay_skip_1d true, 2% linear warmup
comparison.baseline: artifacts/checkpoints-1024-dialogue -- beta2 0.999, weight decay on all params, no warmup
comparison.held_equal: tokens-v4 corpus, seed 5489, batch 64 effective, seq_len 512, ddp 4, size 1024, lr 3e-4, stochastic_rounding true, tt-metal v0.77.0 for the candidate
comparison.NOT_held_equal: The baseline ran on whatever tt-metal was current on 2026-08-18, which was not v0.77.0. So this compares optimizer settings AND a tt-metal version together, and cannot separate them. Stated because the previous attempt at this comparison failed by not checking exactly this kind of thing.

the_noise_floor_that_makes_this_readable.method: Consecutive validations of a SINGLE run, 500 steps apart. If one run's own curve moves by X between adjacent points, a matched delta smaller than X carries no information.
the_noise_floor_that_makes_this_readable.reading: Our own curve moves a median 0.13 between adjacent validations, and rose three times (3000->3500, 4000->4500, 5000->5500). Every matched delta above is at or below that scale, including the -0.183 at step 3000 that briefly looked like a result. It was scatter.

what_this_does_and_does_not_license.keep_weight_decay_skip_1d: YES, on correctness grounds rather than this measurement. Weight decay was being applied to 13 RMSNorm gammas, pulling normalisation gains toward zero, which has no regularising interpretation. That it does not move val loss bounds the size of the effect; it does not make decaying norm gains correct.
what_this_does_and_does_not_license.beta2_0.95: No demonstrated benefit at this scale. Keep or revert on taste. Upstream benchmarked it on TinyLlama, a different size.
what_this_does_and_does_not_license.warmup: Separately measured as no-effect on the same-corpus pair (5.8969 vs 5.9031 at step 1000), and this run does not contradict that. 2% of a 10.7k-step run is ~215 steps.
what_this_does_and_does_not_license.not_licensed: Any claim that the upgrade improved training. It did not, measurably.

process_note: Two earlier attempts at this comparison were void because they trained on artifacts/tokens (the default --tokens-dir, and the oldest of six token sets) rather than tokens-v4. See corpus-provenance.json. train/run.py now writes run_manifest.json so this class of error is self-reporting.

REVISION_2026-08-19_at_8_points.why: The conclusion above was written at SIX matched points and said 'no measurable difference'. That was premature in two ways: I also stated twice that step 6000 was the last matched point, and it was not -- the baseline carries 7000 and 8000.

overall.reading: Mean +0.030 with se 0.036 -- still not distinguishable from zero overall.

the_tail_is_the_result.sign_consistency: 5 of 5 positive; about 6% two-tailed if signs were coin flips
the_tail_is_the_result.reading: From step 4000 onward the v0.77.0 set is consistently WORSE by about 0.08 nats. The overall mean hides this by averaging it against the -0.183 scatter point at step 3000.

REVISION_2026-08-19_at_8_points.revised_answer: Level for the first ~3000 steps, then consistently worse by ~0.08 nats for the rest of the compared range. Marginal, but the sign consistency is what makes it more than scatter.
two_candidate_causes_and_they_are_NOT_se: beta2 0.95 -- a shorter second-moment memory may be less useful once gradients settle, which would show up exactly as a tail effect.
tt-metal v0.77.0 itself -- the dialogue baseline ran on the PRE-v0.77.0 tree. This comparison changes the optimizer AND the tt-metal version together.
REVISION_2026-08-19_at_8_points.the_run_that_separates_them: beta2 0.999 + weight_decay_skip_1d + warmup, on v0.77.0, same corpus and seed, ~35 min at ddp 4. Matching the baseline tail implicates beta2; still-worse implicates tt-metal v0.77.0, which would matter for everything trained afterwards.
REVISION_2026-08-19_at_8_points.practical_size: ~0.08 nats. This project's seed-only noise floor for the behavioural eval suite is 0.1944 nats, and differences inside it are stamped NOT INTERPRETABLE. So this is likely invisible in every downstream eval actually run -- real on the training curve, probably immaterial in behaviour.
REVISION_2026-08-19_at_8_points.consequence: tt-tnt-1024-dialogue REMAINS the designated current model. This run is a recorded candidate that did not win.

FINAL_2026-08-19_at_11_points.supersedes: Both the original six-point conclusion AND the eight-point revision above. Both were wrong, and for the same reason.
FINAL_2026-08-19_at_11_points.what_went_wrong_twice: I printed the baseline curve with `head -8` and then built baselines.json, the monitor, and two written conclusions on that truncation. The baseline has ELEVEN points, running to step 10764. The 'five consecutive positive deltas' that made the tail look real stopped at 8000 because my data stopped at 8000. Steps 9000 and 10000 are NEGATIVE.
FINAL_2026-08-19_at_11_points.answer: No measurable difference. Mean +0.022, standard error 0.029, signs mixed 7 positive / 4 negative with no run longer than five. Every delta sits within the run's own 0.13 median point-to-point wobble.
FINAL_2026-08-19_at_11_points.the_tail_claim_is_WITHDRAWN: There is no consistent late-run disadvantage. tail>=4000 across all eight available points is +0.050 with se 0.028 and signs +++++--+, not the +++++ I reported.
FINAL_2026-08-19_at_11_points.the_isolation_run_is_WITHDRAWN_too: I recommended spending ~35 minutes of hardware on a beta2 0.999 control to explain the tail effect and to separate it from a possible tt-metal v0.77.0 regression. There is no effect to explain. That run would have chased an artifact of my own truncation. Not run.

final_losses.note: The final periodic point (3.0043 at 10764) landed on an upswing; the run's own wobble is +/-0.13, so which side of an oscillation the last validation falls on is not a property of the model.

consequences_unchanged.weight_decay_skip_1d: KEEP -- on correctness grounds, not on this measurement. Decaying 13 RMSNorm gammas toward zero has no regularising interpretation.
consequences_unchanged.beta2_0.95: No demonstrated benefit and now no demonstrated harm. Taste.
consequences_unchanged.designated_model: tt-tnt-1024-dialogue remains current. This candidate matched it; it did not beat it.

FINAL_2026-08-19_at_11_points.the_actual_lesson: Four times in one session a conclusion was driven by a broken instrument rather than by the system under test: a pgrep that matched its own shell, a warmup test one layer below the inertness, a baseline table whose columns collapsed, and now a baseline truncated by head -8. In each case the instrument reported confidently. The measurement discipline this project applies to the model is not yet applied to the tools that measure it.
